notes: Questions name the work, as a researcher asking about a known text would. The v1 set paraphrased each work without its title and measured title-free lexical recall; it remains as a documented retrieval gap, not an admission gate. The Social Contract parent page holds only front matter, so the case expects Book 1 where the argument opens. The Canterbury case expects the prose rendering of the Prologue; Skeat's Middle English edition is an equally valid answer to the question.

cases.question: What limits did King John accept on the power of the English crown in Magna Carta in 1215?
In Dred Scott v. Sandford, could a Black man whose ancestors were brought to America as slaves claim federal citizenship?
In Marbury v. Madison, which 1803 ruling established that courts can declare an act of Congress unconstitutional?
What territory did Mexico cede to the United States under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo?
What protections did the First Geneva Convention of 1864 give to wounded soldiers and medical workers on the battlefield?
What did the Bill of Rights 1689 declare about cruel punishments and excessive bail?
How does The Social Contract begin its argument that people are born free yet everywhere live in chains?
Which pilgrims gather at the Tabard Inn in the Prologue to The Canterbury Tales?
expected_document_titles: Tales from Chaucer/Prologue to the Canterbury Tales

cases.question: What warning did Andrew Jackson give about paper money and the national bank in his Farewell Address?
What rules did the Constitution of the Republic of Texas set for its congress, courts, and voting?
expected_document_titles: Constitution of the Republic of Texas
